chunks: Muhammad ibn Bukran al-Naqqash (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us in Kufa. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, client of Bani Hashim, narrated to us. He said: Al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad informed us. He said: Ahmad ibn Rashid narrated to me from his uncle Sa'id ibn Khuthaym, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali.

He said: I performed Hajj and came to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). He said to me: 'O Abu Hamza! Shall I not tell you about a dream I had? I saw as though I had entered Paradise, and I was brought a houri — I have never seen anyone more beautiful than her. While I was reclining on my couch, I suddenly heard a speaker saying: "O Ali ibn al-Husayn! Congratulations to you on Zayd. O Ali ibn al-Husayn! Congratulations to you on Zayd, congratulations to you on Zayd."'

Abu Hamza said: Then I performed Hajj afterwards and came to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both). I knocked on the door; it was opened for me, and I entered. There he was, carrying Zayd in his arms — or he said: carrying a boy in his arms. He said to me: 'O Abu Hamza, this is the interpretation of my vision from before. My Lord has made it come true.' [12:100]

key_terms.أريكة: A couch or throne, used in descriptions of Paradise in the Quran
key_terms.تأويل: Ta'wil — interpretation or fulfillment of a dream or vision
key_terms.حوراء: A houri — the celestial dark-eyed beauty of Paradise
key_terms.رؤيا: Prophetic dream/vision (ru'ya), regarded in Islamic tradition as one-forty-sixth of prophethood
key_terms.ليهنئك: May it delight/congratulate you — a blessing formula upon joyful news

ai.seo_question: What dream did Imam Zayn al-Abidin have about his son Zayd?
ai.summary: Abu Hamza al-Thumali, a close companion of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), recounts a remarkable incident in two parts. During one Hajj visit, the Imam shared a prophetic dream in which he was in Paradise reclining on a couch when a heavenly voice thrice congratulated him on 'Zayd.' On his next Hajj, Abu Hamza returned to find the Imam holding a newborn son named Zayd, fulfilling the dream exactly. The Imam then quoted the Quranic verse of Prophet Joseph — 'My Lord has made it come true' — linking his own experience of prophetic dreams to the Quranic tradition.
word_analysis: made it / caused it to be

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Bukran al-Niqash (ra) narrated to us in Kufa. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani the servant of Bani Hashim narrated to us. He said: Al-Mundhir b. Muhammad informed us. He said: Ahmad b. Rashid narrated to me from his uncle Sa`id b. Khathim from Abi Hamza al-Thumali.

He said: I went on Hajj, so I met `Ali b. al-Husayn (as), and he said to me: O Aba Hamza! Shall I not tell you about a dream that I had? I saw that it was as though I had entered Paradise, and I was met by a dark-eyed beauty, and I have never seen anyone more beautiful than her. I reclined until I heard a speaker saying: “O `Ali b. al-Husayn! Congratulations to you on Zayd. O `Ali b. al-Husayn! Congratulations to you on Zayd, congratulations to you on Zayd.”

Abu Hamza said: Then, I went on Hajj afterwards. I went to `Ali b. al-Husayn (as) and I knocked on the door. It was opened to me, so I entered. I came across him holding Zayd with his hand – or he said: holding a boy with his hand. So, he said to me: O Aba Hamza, “This is the interpretation of my vision from before. My Lord has made it come true.” [12:100]
